name: pdk-tinode-topic-master-fencing
instr:
# Group topics after master failover

When a cluster master disappears, its group topics move to another node. Today a resumed master can still assign message numbers from stale memory; a failed write can also leave the topic's stored sequence ahead of its messages. Clients then see rejected publishes or holes in room history.

To close this out:

- A group `{pub}` accepted with `{ctrl}` code 202 and `params.seq` is durably stored at that sequence with its original content. The first publish to a new group has sequence 1. Publishers attached to any of three nodes receive distinct, increasing sequence numbers; subscribers receive the live `{data}` stream once, in sequence order. A failed insert is not acknowledged and does not advance the stored topic sequence or leave a hole when publishing resumes.
- After the master is killed, publishing and group subscriptions work again within 15 seconds. Every acknowledged message remains available in history exactly once. An in-flight forwarded request to an unavailable master receives an explicit error within 12 seconds rather than disappearing.
- After a master is paused, another node can take over within 15 seconds. When the former master resumes, it cannot acknowledge publishes as the former owner; stored topic sequence never moves backwards, and the surviving topic continues accepting messages. A later ring move back to that node starts from the latest durable sequence without reuse.
